newsitem.title: USA: Washington plan to 'inflation-proof' college tuition.
newsitem.headline: Washington plan to 'inflation-proof' college tuition.

text.p: Washington state's governor signed a bill Wednesday allowing parents to buy college tuition "units" at current prices as a hedge against inflation for use when their children reach college age.

Gov. Gary Locke, a Democrat, said the new law would "inflation-proof" college tuition for many Washington State residents, making it easier for them to cope with the skyrocketing cost of higher education.

"A college education is too vital to the future of our children to be jeopardised by tuition inflation," Locke said in a statement. "Middle income families will see the doors to our state's colleges and universities opening a bit wider as this measure becomes law."
Bought at current tuition rates, the units would be redeemable at any public college or university in the state in the future, no matter how high tuition fees may rise.

State officials said the units would provide a significant hedge against inflation and tuition increases. Over the past 10 years college and university tuition fees have jumped 100 percent in Washington state, the governor's office said.
Washington's plan would be similar to those offered in several other states. Locke said Washington could begin to operate the programme in the spring of 1998.
Locke said a business plan would be developed for the programme to set the cost of tuition units and to decide whether organisations would be able to buy units for scholarships.
A provision in the tuition legislation would prevent unit holders from selling or exchanging the units for other goods or services.
